clue.text: Union leader comes in to bless deck

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the word union is wanted
to come in is to enter, so this letter goes inside the word for bless

blocks.note: to beatify is to bless, the step before sainthood
first letter of Union

explanation.surface: A trade union boss turns up to bless a ship's deck at a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' looks like a ship's deck but is a verb here, as in deck the halls.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something is to adorn or decorate it, which is a synonym for making it more attractive.

clue.text: A terror on the golf course was Humphrey, so I've heard

definitions.text: A terror on the golf course

indicators.note: something only heard rather than seen is a matter of sound, not spelling

blocks.note: Bogie was the nickname of the film star Humphrey Bogart

explanation.surface: Humphrey Bogart is pictured as a menace on the golf links.
explanation.walkthrough: BOGY is both a bugbear or goblin (a terror) and a spelling of bogey, the golfer's score of one over par.
explanation.definitionFit: A bogy is a frightening spectre, and on the links a bogey score is what golfers dread most.

clue.text: Shaw said to be a culture vulture?

definitions.note: a phrase describing someone, matching the adjective

indicators.note: something said is spoken aloud, so we want a word sounding like the name

blocks.note: Artie Shaw was an American swing bandleader and clarinettist

explanation.surface: Is Bernard Shaw rumoured to be a snob about the arts?
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw suggests George Bernard Shaw, but the Shaw needed is the bandleader Artie Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone arty shows a showy, perhaps pretentious enthusiasm for the arts, exactly what a culture vulture has.

clue.text: He wrote, after his time, about some hot potato

definitions.text: He wrote, after his time, about some hot potato

blocks.clueFragment: He wrote, after his time, about some hot potato
blocks.note: surface reading: a journalist writing late about a touchy issue
setter's reading: a Victorian novelist whose later books were scandalous and controversial

explanation.surface: A writer covered a controversial issue only after it had passed.
explanation.walkthrough: The novelist of Tess and Jude the Obscure, a book so controversial it was burnt; he went on writing poetry well into the twentieth century. No tighter wordplay for the letters has been found.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dorset author's novels caused outrage on publication, making them a literary hot potato of their era.

clue.text: Designer for use at work at a table

blocks.note: a function is the use something serves when working
the article, with at joining
a table of items is a list

explanation.surface: Someone designing furniture meant for practical use at a working table.
explanation.definitionFit: A functionalist is an architect or designer who holds that form should follow purpose, so it names a kind of designer.

clue.text: Group to be followed by UEU

blocks.clueFragment: Group to be followed by UEU
blocks.note: surface reading: a band billed ahead of an act named UEU
setter's reading: a group of six, such as the closing lines of a sonnet

explanation.surface: A band is told it will be succeeded on stage by an act called UEU.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'Group' clearly defines; what 'to be followed by UEU' contributes is unexplained, and the clue may be damaged in this copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sestet is a set of six, especially six musicians or the last six lines of a sonnet.

clue.text: Celestial quarter where duck swallows lady

indicators.note: what swallows something takes it inside, so the bird's name encloses the other word

blocks.note: east, one of the four compass quarters
the teal is a small duck
a lady is a her

explanation.surface: A part of a pond where a duck gulps down a woman, oddly called heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarter' is not a district but one of the four points of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means of the upper air or heavens, so it is a synonym for heavenly or celestial.

clue.text: Sailor, one to cheat and lie

blocks.note: a tar is a sailor
one as the article a
to diddle someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: A seaman sets out to swindle and deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: A taradiddle is a petty falsehood or fib, so the word is a synonym for a lie.

clue.text: Playing by ear during attempts with soft fruit

indicators.note: playing by ear is improvising, so the letters are freely rearranged
what happens during something sits within it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: the letters of by ear rearranged
attempts are tries

explanation.surface: A musician improvises tunes through several attempts while eating fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The mixed letters sit after the T of TRIES: T-AYBER-RIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tayberries are a raspberry and blackberry hybrid, an example of soft summer fruit.

clue.text: Become familiar with single race area without high king at present

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is dropped from the area

blocks.note: a ghetto is a district occupied by one ethnic group
H is the abbreviation for high
K for king, as in chess
at present means now

explanation.surface: An area for one race, minus a high king, is something to learn about now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' governs only 'high'; the king is then added, not removed.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to know someone is to become acquainted with them, the same idiom in other words.

clue.text: The very first performance of the "Emperor", Wilder version

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The debut of Beethoven's Emperor concerto in a wilder interpretation.
explanation.definitionFit: A world premiere is the first public performance of a work anywhere, so it is literally the very first showing.

clue.text: See 3
3 11's place for sugar with game

blocks.note: caster sugar is a fine-grained white sugar
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A place where sugar goes with a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 11 is Thomas Hardy, and caster sugar is the British name for superfine sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Casterbridge is the fictional Wessex town, modelled on Dorchester, in the novels of the Dorset author.

clue.text: Veto on one, with the monarch intervening, sent into exile

indicators.note: to intervene is to come between, so the royal letters go inside the next word

blocks.note: a veto is a ban
one as the Roman numeral I
taken as written
HM stands for His or Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A banned person, after royal intervention, is packed off abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent' looks like part of the definition but is wordplay; only 'exile' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Banishment is the state of being expelled from one's country, which is a synonym for exile.

clue.text: Biased account supplied by idiots to Royal Navy

indicators.note: read as supple-y, bent into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
RN is the abbreviation for the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Fools handed the Navy a one-sided version of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supplied' looks like simply provided, but is read as made supple, the signal to mix the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A distortion is a misleading, slanted representation of the facts, so it fits a biased account.

clue.text: A lot of policemen take drugs

definitions.note: plural, while the answer names one drug

blocks.note: taken as written
the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: Many police officers are using narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' looks like a quantity but splits: A, then the lot (body) of policemen.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid is slang for LSD, a hallucinogen, so it is an example of the drugs in question.

clue.text: One of 3 11's people, funny old article seen in amazement

blocks.note: the letters of old mixed up
the indefinite article
wonder is amazement

explanation.walkthrough: The Woodlanders is a Thomas Hardy novel set among Dorset forest folk.
explanation.definitionFit: The Woodlanders is Thomas Hardy's novel about forest dwellers, so a woodlander is one of its people.

clue.text: Old sailor in a groove has a drink - upset inside

taken as written
nog is a strong ale or eggnog

explanation.walkthrough: The overturned drink goes into the groove just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argonauts sailed with Jason on the Argo, so an Argonaut is a mythical sailor of ancient times.

clue.text: Cross-fertilise, perhaps - try near rim?

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: There is no word signalling the mix; the question mark invites trying the three words in another order.
explanation.definitionFit: Intermarry means to marry outside one's group, which is a human form of crossbreeding or cross-fertilising.

clue.text: Illness reported - I must let some air in

definitions.text: I must let some air in

indicators.note: a report is spoken, so the word sounds like the illness

blocks.note: flu, short for influenza

explanation.surface: A sick person reports feeling ill and wants a window opened.
explanation.definitionFit: A flue is a chimney duct, which must draw in air for the fire to burn: the definition is the flue speaking.

clue.text: Dome scene, 10 with a commercial turn

the article in its other form
an ad is a commercial
a U-turn

explanation.definitionFit: In Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan, Xanadu is where the stately pleasure-dome was decreed.

clue.text: Damage coin that's damaged at base by an arithmetical concept

the letters of coin rearranged

clue.text: One with pride at being a celebrity

second meaning: a famous person sought after socially

explanation.definitionFit: A pride is a group of the big cats, and a lion is also a celebrated person, as in a literary lion.

clue.text: Joint complaint?

blocks.note: first meaning: a joint of meat from cattle
second meaning: a grievance, slang

taken as written
